key_insight: A deep learning surrogate can replace expensive CPFE simulations to optimize polycrystalline microstructures for competing quasi-static and dynamic strength targets.
engineering_relevance: This enables fast, full-field design optimization of microstructures while preserving the physics needed to assess spall, yield, and wave-driven failure behavior.
method: 3D U-Net maps 3D polycrystalline microstructures to full-field velocity histories from plate-impact simulations.
Couples stochastic microstructure generation with derivative-free optimization to search the design space efficiently.
Uses a distribution-consistent reliability region (DCRR) based on MMD to detect surrogate shift during optimization.
evidence_signal: Validated optimal designs against CPFE with less than 3% prediction error, while reducing cumulative optimization time by about four orders of magnitude.
watch_item: Reliability depends on the surrogate staying within the training-data distribution, so distribution shift must be monitored carefully during optimization.
paper_title: Deep learning driven framework for optimization of polycrystalline microstructures under competing strength requirements
